author: P. M. Nelson
title: Illinois Institute of Technology accepts 55% of applicants for fall 2024 entering class
text:
Schools
Illinois Institute of Technology accepts 55% of applicants for fall 2024 entering class
Illinois Institute of Technology received 12,216 applications and admitted 55% of applicants to the fall 2024 entering class, the National Center for Education Statistics reported.
Illinois Institute of Technology received 12,216 applications for the fall 2024 entering class and admitted 55% of applicants, according to the National Center for Education Statistics.
The reported yield—the share of admitted applicants who enrolled—was 8%. The university enrolled 519 first-time undergraduates.
These figures reflect first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduates, not Illinois Institute of Technology's total enrollment.
For the fall 2024 cohort, the middle 50% of enrolled first-time undergraduates who submitted SAT scores reported reading and writing section scores ranging from 590 to 720 and math section scores ranging from 590 to 720, with 30% of enrolled first-time undergraduates submitting SAT scores. The ACT composite range for the middle 50% of enrolled first-time undergraduates who submitted scores was 26 to 32, submitted by 8% of enrolled first-time undergraduates.
The acceptance rate was unchanged from the prior year.
Across U.S. postsecondary institutions that participate in federal student aid programs and do not have open-admissions policies, 59% of first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate applicants were admitted for fall 2024, according to provisional National Center for Education Statistics data. Because the figures are aggregated across institutions, students who apply to or are admitted by multiple colleges may be counted more than once.
The average cost of college in the United States has more than doubled in the 21st century, rising by about 4% each year, with published tuition and fees at private nonprofit four-year institutions averaging more than $38,000 a year.
